text: By 1936 the books were selling, but the returns and the printing bills ran ahead of us. A debt is a siege, friend. It only tightens.

Donenfeld printed my books and carried my debts. When I needed money for Detective Comics, he offered it, at the price of a partnership. I signed. A man with creditors at the door does not haggle long.

choices.text: That sounds like you had no real choice.
So you made a bad business deal?

text: So Detective Comics, Inc. was born, with Donenfeld and his accountant, Jack Liebowitz, as my partners. I had the ideas. They had the ledgers.
A bad deal? Perhaps. You try haggling with a man who holds every one of your debts. I dare say you would have signed too.
By 1938 I was out. Sued, bankrupt, and the company sold to Donenfeld's outfit. That is the short of it.

choices.text: Is there more to the story?
What became of the company after you?

text: He paid for a cruise. Go to Cuba, rest, come back with new ideas, he said. I came home to a locked office and a stack of lawyers' papers. I have been shot at, and that still stung worse.

choices.text: Did you ever see Superman's success coming?
